explanation.not_claimed: This is an assumption-conditioned border-value accounting exposure for one annual accounting period. It is not a GDP loss, welfare change, fiscal revenue, consumer inflation, unemployment, oil demand elasticity or balance-of-payments forecast, and it has no general-equilibrium closure.
explanation.sign_convention: net_external_cost_change_usd = import_value_change_usd − export_value_change_usd. Positive means a higher net external payment for crude under the stated assumptions; negative net cost indicates net receipt exposure (exports gain more value than imports cost).
explanation.uncertainty: Unquantified: the sources publish no uncertainty for M, X or G and no justified error model is introduced. In an L2 run the min/max over the elasticity grid together with the fixed-quantity point ε=(0,0) is published as a separate row: a sensitivity range, not a confidence interval (assumption sensitivity, no coverage level); the L1 value keeps its unquantified status.

explanation.sign_convention: net_external_cost_change_usd = import_value_change_usd − export_value_change_usd. Positive means a higher net external payment for crude under the stated assumptions; negative net cost indicates net receipt exposure (exports gain more value than imports cost).

assumptions: same-year source-reported border values and nominal GDP, all in current USD
imports commonly CIF and exports FOB; the provider-declared basis of each value is kept
one annual accounting period; no dynamics
fixed quantities (L1)
no general equilibrium, exchange-rate, fiscal or second-round effects
a headline crude benchmark price change is not automatically this border-price intervention
explanation.not_claimed: This is an assumption-conditioned border-value accounting exposure for one annual accounting period. It is not a GDP loss, welfare change, fiscal revenue, consumer inflation, unemployment, oil demand elasticity or balance-of-payments forecast, and it has no general-equilibrium closure.
explanation.sign_convention: net_external_cost_change_usd = import_value_change_usd − export_value_change_usd. Positive means a higher net external payment for crude under the stated assumptions; negative net cost indicates net receipt exposure (exports gain more value than imports cost).
explanation.uncertainty: Unquantified: the sources publish no uncertainty for M, X or G and no justified error model is introduced. In an L2 run the min/max over the elasticity grid together with the fixed-quantity point ε=(0,0) is published as a separate row: a sensitivity range, not a confidence interval (assumption sensitivity, no coverage level); the L1 value keeps its unquantified status.

units.export_value_change_usd: current US dollars over one annual accounting period
units.exposure_percent_baseline_gdp: percent of same-year baseline nominal GDP (current USD)
units.import_value_change_usd: current US dollars over one annual accounting period
units.net_external_cost_change_usd: current US dollars over one annual accounting period
